auth.title: API key
highlights:
# API key

## What is an API key

API key is an identity of your LiveAgent (like your username and password) which you can use to build your own custom integration solutions. Never give it to anybody you don't trust. If your API key is lost, do not hesitate to generate a new one! Anybody with your API key can fully access your LiveAgent.

## How can I get my API key

While logged in as an admin navigate to Configuration> System> API which loads the API v3 section where you find existing API keys or add a new one. To access the API v1 section click the Settings for API v1 link under the API v3 header.

This is how the API v1 section looks where you have settings for your API v1 key.

When adding a new API key in v3 you have an option to define permissions for this key (as you can have more keys you can also give different keys to different people with different permissions).

## Can I change the API key?

Yes both API versions have options to generate new keys and invalidate existing ones.

IMPORTANT NOTE: Do not forget that when you generate a new API key for your LiveAgent ALL clients using the old key will stop working immediately!

## API v3 use

Your API key has to be set in header of your requests:

curl --location --request GET 'https://your.ladesk.com/api/v3/tickets' \  --header 'apikey: 0865evv883j6auflvlt7zrwgqn32qo74' \  --header 'Content-Type: application/json'

Here's an example of cURL code in PHP:

```
curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, array('Accept: application/json', 'apikey: 123456_YOUR_API_KEY_123456'));
```

 Updated: Mar 16, 2021

auth.title: LiveAgent API v1 vs v3: Authentication Differences, API Key Management, and Resolving 403 Errors
highlights:
## Understanding the Two API Versions

LiveAgent supports two API versions:

- API v1 – A legacy (deprecated) version. No new endpoints are being added, but it remains functional and can be used alongside API v3.
- API v3 – The current, actively developed version. New endpoints and enhancements are continuously added.

Both versions can be used simultaneously, but they require separate API keys. Using an API v3 key to authenticate against API v1 endpoints (or vice versa) will result in a 403 ApiKey not found error.

## How to Obtain the Correct API Key

### API v3 Key

1. Log in to your LiveAgent account.
2. Navigate to Configuration > System > API.
3. Generate or manage your API v3 key here.
4. Ensure the key has the appropriate permissions assigned for the operations you intend to perform (e.g., reading or posting messages).

### API v1 Key

1. Log in to your LiveAgent account.
2. In the upper right corner of the API configuration page, switch to the Settings for API v1 section.
3. Obtain your API v1 key from this section.

## Troubleshooting: 403 "ApiKey not found" Error

If you receive a 403 ApiKey not found response when calling an API endpoint, the most common cause is using the wrong API key for the API version you are targeting. Follow these steps to resolve it:

- Confirm which API version the endpoint belongs to (v1 or v3).
- Make sure you are using the matching API key for that version.
- Verify that the API key has the required permissions for the specific operation (e.g., posting messages to a conversation).

## API Permissions

When using API v3, permissions are managed per API key under Configuration > System > API. Ensure the key is granted the relevant scopes for the actions you want to perform, such as reading tickets or posting messages.

For API v1, authentication is handled via the v1-specific key obtained from the Settings for API v1 section. Make sure the agent account associated with the key has the appropriate role and access rights within LiveAgent.

auth.title: MCP Integration for agents
highlights:
# MCP Integration for agents

LiveAgent exposes a built-in MCP server (Model Context Protocol) that lets you connect external AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Cursor, claude.ai, FlowHunt, or any other MCP-compatible client, directly with your LiveAgent account. Once connected, your own AI tools/agents can read ticket data and perform actions on your behalf, using your agent identity and permissions.

There are two ways to authenticate your MCP client - OAuth 2.1 (recommended), where the AI tool discovers the authorization server automatically and redirects you to a consent screen, or Bearer token, where you generate an MCP access token in your profile and paste it into the AI tool's configuration manually.

## Finding MCP Integration in your profile

1. Click your avatar in the top-right corner of the LiveAgent panel and select Edit profile.
2. In the left-hand menu, navigate to the MCP Integration section.

This screen shows your connection details and access tokens. Use these values to configure any MCP-compatible client:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| MCP server URL | https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp |
| Transport protocol | Streamable HTTP |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE) or Bearer token |

## Connecting with OAuth

OAuth authentication lets AI tools connect to your LiveAgent MCP server without you having to generate, copy, and paste a token. The tool handles the entire authentication flow automatically using standard OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.

### How it works

1. In your AI tool (for example Claude app), add a new MCP server/connector/plugin using your LiveAgent MCP server URL.
2. The AI tool calls that URL, receives a discovery hint, and fetches LiveAgent's OAuth server metadata automatically.
3. You are redirected to the LiveAgent login page (if not already logged in) and then to a consent screen asking you to approve the connection.
4. After you approve, the tool receives an access token and is ready to use.

Note: Your consent decision is remembered. If you remove and reconnect the same tool later, the consent screen is skipped and completes silently.

### Managing authorized apps

The MCP Integration screen in your profile lists all OAuth clients you have approved under Authorized apps. You can revoke any authorized app. The tool will lose access immediately and will need to go through the OAuth flow again to reconnect.

Tip: Administrators or users with a custom role with the permission to manage agents can view and revoke authorized apps for other agents in the account.

...

auth.title: API v1 vs. API v3 in LiveAgent: Key Differences, Authentication, and Resolving ApiKey Errors
highlights:
## Understanding API v1 and API v3 Keys

LiveAgent supports two API versions — API v1 (deprecated, but still functional) and API v3 (current, actively developed). These two versions use separate API keys and are managed in different places. Using an API v3 key against an API v1 endpoint (or vice versa) will result in authentication errors such as `403 ApiKey not found`.

## How to Obtain Your API Key

### API v3 Key

1. Log in to your LiveAgent account.
2. Navigate to Configuration > System > API.
3. Generate a new API key or copy an existing one.
4. Make sure the key has the appropriate permissions assigned for the endpoints you intend to use (e.g., read/write access to conversations or tickets).

### API v1 Key

1. Go to the Configuration > System > API page.
2. In the upper right corner of the API settings page, switch to the "Settings for API v1" section.
3. Obtain your API v1 key from that section.

## Common Error: `403 ApiKey not found`

This error typically occurs when:

- You are using an API v3 key to authenticate against an API v1 endpoint (or vice versa).
- The API key has insufficient permissions for the requested operation.
- The API key is invalid or has been revoked.

Solution: Ensure you are using the correct key for the API version you are targeting. If you are calling API v3 endpoints (e.g., `POST /api/conversations/{conversationId}/messages`), use your API v3 key with the required permissions configured. If you are calling API v1 endpoints, use your API v1 key obtained from the "Settings for API v1" section.

## Posting Messages via API v3: Ticket ID vs. Conversation ID

gate.title: API features | LiveAgent
highlights:
# API

LiveAgent’s API enables seamless software communication, supporting actions like company retrieval and conversation creation. Integrate with tools via Zapier, access resources like demos, and enhance customer support with features like collaboration tools and iOS app.

## What is an API?

An API (Application Programming Interface) is a list of commands that one software can send to another. Thanks to API you can reconnect multiple programs, tools, and automate and influence many tasks. Two different software can “communicate” directly via API.

## How does LiveAgent’s API work?

LiveAgent’s API enables seamless software communication, allowing you to send information from or into your LiveAgent account from other apps via API. This means you can automate tasks, streamline workflows, and connect your favorite tools without manual intervention.

...

## Available LiveAgent API Actions

LiveAgent’s API supports a wide range of actions to help you automate your customer support operations:

- Retrieve the list of companies
- Delete conversations
- Create new conversations
- Register new customers
- Retrieve the list of departments
- Remove knowledge base entries
- Generate department reports
- And many more…

## Connecting AI Tools Instead of Custom Code

If you want an AI client like Claude Desktop to work with your tickets directly, rather than building a custom integration on top of the API, LiveAgent’s MCP server gives it a standardized, permission-scoped way to search, tag, and act on tickets.

...

Do I need technical knowledge to use the API? 

While the API is powerful and flexible, you can also use Zapier for no-code integrations with hundreds of popular tools. For more advanced integrations, technical knowledge may be helpful, but LiveAgent provides comprehensive API documentation and support.

mcp.title: Connect AI tools to LiveAgent with MCP
highlights:
# Connect AI tools to LiveAgent with MCP

Let ChatGPT, Claude and other MCP-compatible AI clients search, tag, and act on your tickets directly — inside the same permissions your agents already have.

## A standard way for AI tools to plug into your help desk

MCP is an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools and data. LiveAgent's MCP server exposes tickets, ticket messages, knowledge base articles, agents, and departments as tools an MCP-compatible AI client can call directly — no custom integration required.

-  Search and read tickets, messages, and knowledge base articles
-  Tag, assign, transfer, resolve, and reopen tickets
-  List agents and departments to route work correctly
-  Reply to WhatsApp conversations where enabled

   MCP Server · Claude Desktop

 Claude Desktop Connected

 search_tickets Idle  Called  get_ticket_messages Idle  Called  add_tags_to_ticket Idle  Called  resolve_ticket Idle  Called

mcp.connect({ client: “Claude Desktop”, tools: “33”, scope: “tickets kb agents” })

## MCP server

### Built for teams already using an AI client

If your team already relies on Claude Desktop or another MCP-compatible AI client day-to-day, connect it once and let it work with live ticket data instead of a static export.

What your AI client can help with:

- Triage and tag incoming tickets
- Summarize long ticket threads on request
- Look up knowledge base answers while chatting with you
- Route tickets to the right department

### Access stays inside your existing permissions

Connecting an AI client isn't an all-access step. It uses an access token you generate in your own profile, or an OAuth 2.1 sign-in with a consent screen, so it always acts as one account you approved.

What stays under your control:

- Every ticket action is checked against that account's department and role permissions
- Access tokens are scoped to approved actions, not blanket account access
- Individual tools, like WhatsApp replies, can be turned off

...

## Every tool your AI client can call

LiveAgent’s MCP server gives a connected AI client 33 tools to work with, covering tickets, custom fields, the knowledge base, and more. Every tool still respects the connecting account’s own department and role permissions, so an AI client never sees or does more than the agent it’s acting as.

## Tickets

| What it does for you | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Finds tickets matching a keyword, status, or other filter, so your AI client can pull up the right one without you searching manually | `search_tickets` |
| Reads a ticket’s full conversation, message by message, so it has real context before doing anything | `get_ticket_messages` |
| Checks a ticket’s details — status, channel, and other metadata | `get_ticket_metadata` |
| Sees what tags exist on the account | `get_tags` |
| Adds a tag to a ticket | `add_tags_to_ticket` |
| Removes a tag from a ticket | `remove_tags_from_ticket` |
| Assigns a ticket to an agent | `assign_ticket` |
| Moves a ticket to another department | `transfer_ticket` |
| Resolves a ticket | `resolve_ticket` |
| Reopens a resolved ticket | `reopen_ticket` |
| Flags a ticket as spam | `mark_as_spam` |
| Clears a spam flag that shouldn’t be there | `mark_as_not_spam` |
| Adds an internal note that only agents see, not the customer | `add_note` |
| Reads back a ticket’s existing internal notes | `get_ticket_notes` |

## Custom ticket fields

| What it does for you | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Shows what custom fields your account has set up | `get_ticket_field_definitions` |
| Reads the values already filled in on a ticket | `get_ticket_field_values` |
| Fills in or updates a field’s value — creates it if it isn’t set yet | `set_ticket_field_value` |
| Clears a field’s value | `delete_ticket_field_value` |

## AI-generated content

| What it does for you | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Checks if a ticket already has an AI summary, and reads it if so | `get_ticket_summary` |
| Generates and saves a new summary for a ticket | `submit_ticket_summary` |
| Drafts a reply for an agent to review before sending, instead of sending it directly | `submit_answer_suggestion` |
| Submits polished or AI-edited text for the answer assistant to use | `submit_text_modification` |

## Knowledge base

| What it does for you | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Lists the knowledge bases (customer portals) on your account | `list_knowledge_bases` |
| Browses categories as a tree, the same structure customers see | `list_kb_categories` |
| Searches articles by keyword | `search_kb_articles` |
| Reads one article in full | `get_kb_article` |
| Writes a new article | `create_kb_article` |
| Updates an existing article | `update_kb_article` |
| Creates a category to keep articles organized | `create_kb_category` |
| Updates an existing category | `update_kb_category` |

## Team lookups

| What it does for you | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Lists your agents, so the AI client can route work to the right person instead of guessing | `list_agents` |
| Lists your departments, so the AI client can route work to the right team instead of guessing | `list_departments` |

## Channel-specific

| What it does for you | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Replies to a customer on WhatsApp — only while the 24-hour customer-service window is open, and only for the conversation the AI client is already handling, so it can’t jump into a different customer’s chat | `reply_via_whatsapp` |

...

What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)? 

MCP is an open standard that lets AI applications, such as ChatGPT and Claude, connect securely to outside tools and data sources. Instead of copying and pasting information back and forth, an MCP-compatible AI client can read and act on data directly, inside the permissions you grant it.

 What is LiveAgent's MCP server? 

LiveAgent's MCP server lets you connect an MCP-compatible AI client, like ChatGPT or Claude, directly to your LiveAgent account. Once connected, the AI client can search tickets, read conversations, add tags, and take other actions you've approved, without an agent copying data between apps.

 What can a connected AI tool do in LiveAgent? 

A connected AI tool can search and read tickets, view ticket messages and knowledge base articles, tag, assign, transfer, resolve, and reopen tickets, list agents and departments, and reply to WhatsApp conversations where that channel is enabled. Every action still respects the permissions of the account it connects as.

 How is access secured? 

There are two ways to connect an AI client: an MCP access token you generate in your LiveAgent profile, or, for clients that support it such as claude.ai, an OAuth 2.1 sign-in with a consent screen where you approve which account the AI client acts as. Access tokens are scoped, and every ticket-level action is checked against that account's own department and role permissions before it runs.

 Which AI clients work with LiveAgent's MCP server? 

ChatGPT, Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code), Cursor and any other AI client that supports the Model Context Protocol can connect. The connection is built on the open MCP standard rather than a single vendor's client, so new MCP-compatible tools work too.

 Which plans include the MCP server? 

The Business and Enterprise plans, and the free 30-day trial.

mcp.title: MCP Integration for agents
highlights:
# MCP Integration for agents

LiveAgent exposes a built-in MCP server (Model Context Protocol) that lets you connect external AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Cursor, claude.ai, FlowHunt, or any other MCP-compatible client, directly with your LiveAgent account. Once connected, your own AI tools/agents can read ticket data and perform actions on your behalf, using your agent identity and permissions.

There are two ways to authenticate your MCP client - OAuth 2.1 (recommended), where the AI tool discovers the authorization server automatically and redirects you to a consent screen, or Bearer token, where you generate an MCP access token in your profile and paste it into the AI tool's configuration manually.

## Finding MCP Integration in your profile

1. Click your avatar in the top-right corner of the LiveAgent panel and select Edit profile.
2. In the left-hand menu, navigate to the MCP Integration section.

This screen shows your connection details and access tokens. Use these values to configure any MCP-compatible client:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| MCP server URL | https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp |
| Transport protocol | Streamable HTTP |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE) or Bearer token |

## Connecting with OAuth

OAuth authentication lets AI tools connect to your LiveAgent MCP server without you having to generate, copy, and paste a token. The tool handles the entire authentication flow automatically using standard OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.

### How it works

1. In your AI tool (for example Claude app), add a new MCP server/connector/plugin using your LiveAgent MCP server URL.
2. The AI tool calls that URL, receives a discovery hint, and fetches LiveAgent's OAuth server metadata automatically.
3. You are redirected to the LiveAgent login page (if not already logged in) and then to a consent screen asking you to approve the connection.
4. After you approve, the tool receives an access token and is ready to use.

Note: Your consent decision is remembered. If you remove and reconnect the same tool later, the consent screen is skipped and completes silently.

### Managing authorized apps

The MCP Integration screen in your profile lists all OAuth clients you have approved under Authorized apps. You can revoke any authorized app. The tool will lose access immediately and will need to go through the OAuth flow again to reconnect.

Tip: Administrators or users with a custom role with the permission to manage agents can view and revoke authorized apps for other agents in the account.

## Connecting with a bearer token

If your AI tool does not support OAuth authentication, you can use a bearer token to connect it. Bearer tokens are MCP access tokens you generate in your profile and paste directly into your MCP client. Bearer tokens are also used by scripts that require manual configuration.

### Generating an access token

1. On the MCP Integration screen in your profile and click Generate token.
2. Copy the access token.
3. Paste the access token into your MCP client as the Bearer token value.

Important: Store the access token securely as soon as you generate it. If you lose it, you will need to revoke the existing token and generate a new one.

You can generate up to 10 active access tokens per account. Having multiple tokens is useful if you connect the same account to more than one tool or device.

### Managing access tokens

The access token list on the MCP Integration screen shows each token's masked identifier and expiration date. Each can be revoked independently without affecting the others. Upon revoking a token, the corresponding MCP client/AI tool will lose access immediately.

Note: Access tokens expire automatically after two years from the date they were generated, regardless of how frequently they are used. Plan to rotate access tokens before they expire to avoid interruption.

## Permissions and available tools

Regardless of whether you connect via OAuth or bearer token, your AI tool has access to the full set of LiveAgent MCP tools. See the MCP tools reference for the complete list of tools and their detailed description.

All actions are performed under your agent identity and are subject to your role's permissions, exactly as if you had performed them in the LiveAgent panel. They appear in the ticket's activity history under your name.

Note: Unlike LiveAgent AI agents, which restrict the tool set per AI agent configuration, personal MCP integration gives access to all tools. Your role's permissions still apply - actions your role is not permitted to perform will be rejected.

Note: Actions performed through an MCP connection count toward a common AI budget shared by all users, which limits the number of tool calls. See the AI budgets article for details on how AI budgets work.

mcp.title: MCP tools reference
highlights:
# MCP tools reference

This article documents the tools exposed by the LiveAgent MCP server, including the exact parameters each tool accepts and the exact fields it returns. A personal MCP connection offers every tool the agent's role has the privileges for, while an AI agent MCP connection offers only the tools selected for that AI agent.

Every tool returns a single JSON object. A call that succeeds returns the documented response, while a tool that has nothing to return answers with `{"success": true}`. A call that fails or is refused returns an error object, e.g. `{"success": false, "error": "Not authorized to read this ticket"}` or `{"code": -32602, "message": "Tool is not available on this account: reply_via_whatsapp"}`. That usually happens when the tool is not enabled for the AI agent, the tool is not available to AI agents at all, an AI agent names a ticket other than the one its run was started for, the agent's role lacks a privilege the tool needs, the tool is not available on the account, a usage limit is reached, etc.

Two rules apply to every AI agent connection:

- Every tool that takes a `ticketId` is locked to the ticket the AI agent's run was started for — reading messages and notes, tags, ticket fields, status changes, assignment, transfer and replies alike. A call that names any other ticket is refused.
- The knowledge base tools give an AI agent public content only: knowledge bases with an active customer portal, public categories, and articles that are both published and public. Anything else is reported as not found. An AI agent can also create or move articles and categories only into categories it can see, and once it creates or changes an article or category as draft or internal, it can no longer read or edit it. Personal MCP connections see all content, drafts and internal items included.

## Read-only tools

These tools look up tickets, account data and knowledge base content without changing anything.

### Search tickets (search_tickets)

Retrieves the tickets that match the given filters, most recently changed first. Each call returns up to 10 tickets by default, or up to 50 with `limit` — page through the rest with `nextCursor`. This tool is available through personal MCP connections only — AI agents cannot use it.

mcp.title: AI Agents feature overview
highlights:
The AI Agents feature allows you to create reusable AI-powered agents and trigger them via automatic rules. AI agents utilize the built-in MCP server and its tools to perform various actions within your LiveAgent account. They serve as a background automation layer alongside other LiveAgent AI-powered features.

Note: To use the AI Agents feature, it is required to integrate your LiveAgent account with an AI provider, and set the feature up.  It is recommended to integrate FlowHunt as your AI provider and set up your AI agents via it to have full control over the workflow and troubleshooting.

...

## How it works

An AI agent is the central configuration object. It tells the system which AI provider to call, how it should process ticket(s), and which actions it is allowed to perform. One agent per use case (e.g., one for auto-tagging, one for ticket triage/categorization, one for generating knowledge base articles from resolved tickets, etc.) is the recommended approach. One AI agent can be reused in many automatic rules, and each AI agent has its own AI provider and model.

When an automatic rule containing the action "Run AI agent" triggers, the system dispatches the AI agent to your AI provider, which processes the ticket and performs actions it is allowed to do, such as tagging the ticket, resolving it, assigning it to an agent, transferring it to another department, or writing a knowledge base article out of it - all without any human intervention.

LiveAgent exposes a built-in MCP server (model context protocol) that your AI provider connects to when executing an AI agent. When the AI provider needs to read ticket data or perform an action, it calls an MCP server endpoint, and LiveAgent executes the corresponding tool. Every tool call is authenticated and validated before it reaches the ticket.

...

Tools that are not allowed for a given AI agent are unavailable to the AI provider, even if the underlying provider would request them.
